title: EDL
description: The deterministic edit plan for one video output. Every creative decision in the finished film or reel is expressed here; the renderer executes it and decides nothing.
$comment:
=====================================================================
 OPENTIMELINEIO MAPPING -- READ BEFORE CHANGING ANY FIELD IN THIS FILE
=====================================================================

 Requirement: an EDL must be losslessly exportable to OpenTimelineIO, so a
 pro user can open our auto-cut in Resolve or Premiere and finish it by hand.
 'Losslessly' here means: export to .otio, re-import, and get a byte-identical
 EDL back. Two rules make that achievable.

 RULE 1 -- Structure maps onto OTIO natives, never onto metadata.
 Anything OTIO models natively (clips, gaps, transitions, time, speed,
 markers, media references) uses the OTIO shape exactly, including its
 half-open TimeRange convention and its RationalTime value/rate pair. This is
 why nothing in this contract stores seconds as a float: 30000/1001 has no
 float representation that survives a round trip, and a drifting frame is a
 missed beat.

 RULE 2 -- Everything else round-trips through one metadata namespace.
 Beat grids, story arcs, reframe keyframe tracks and ducking rules have no
 OTIO equivalent. They are written into the OTIO `metadata` dict under the
 single key "memory_engine", which OTIO preserves verbatim across read/write
 and which every NLE ignores safely. An importer reconstructs the EDL from
 that namespace; an editor who never looks at it still gets a correct cut.

 FIELD-BY-FIELD MAPPING

 EDL                          -> otio.schema.Timeline
  .name                       ->   Timeline.name
  .global_start_time          ->   Timeline.global_start_time (RationalTime)
  .tracks[]                   ->   Timeline.tracks (a Stack of Tracks)
  .story_arc                  ->   Timeline.metadata.memory_engine.story_arc
                                   (+ one Marker per act on the arc track,
                                    for editor visibility only -- the
                                    authoritative copy is the metadata)
  .beat_grid                  ->   Timeline.metadata.memory_engine.beat_grid
                                   (+ one Marker per downbeat, same rule)
  .audio_plan.ducking         ->   Timeline.metadata.memory_engine.ducking
  .audio_plan.mix             ->   Timeline.metadata.memory_engine.mix
  .reframe_tracks[]           ->   Timeline.metadata.memory_engine.reframe_tracks
  .determinism                ->   Timeline.metadata.memory_engine.determinism
  .variant                    ->   Timeline.metadata.memory_engine.variant
  .target                     ->   Timeline.metadata.memory_engine.target

 Track                        -> otio.schema.Track
  .kind                       ->   Track.kind ("Video" | "Audio")
  .name                       ->   Track.name
  .items[]                    ->   Track (children list, in order)

 Clip (item_type="clip")      -> otio.schema.Clip
  .name                       ->   Clip.name
  .source_range               ->   Clip.source_range (TimeRange, half-open)
  .media_ref_id -> MediaRef   ->   Clip.media_reference (ExternalReference)
  .enabled                    ->   Clip.enabled
  .markers[]                  ->   Clip.markers[] (otio.schema.Marker)
  .time_effect (linear_speed) ->   Clip.effects += otio.schema.LinearTimeWarp
                                     (time_scalar)
  .time_effect (freeze)       ->   Clip.effects += otio.schema.FreezeFrame
  .color_ops[]                ->   Clip.effects += otio.schema.Effect with
                                     effect_name "memory_engine.color" and the
                                     op in its metadata
  .moment_id, .beat_lock,
  .reframe_track_id,
  .source_media_id            ->   Clip.metadata.memory_engine.*

 Gap (item_type="gap")        -> otio.schema.Gap
  .duration                   ->   Gap.source_range.duration

 Transition                   -> otio.schema.Transition
  (item_type="transition")
  .transition_type            ->   Transition.transition_type
                                   ("SMPTE_Dissolve" | "Custom")
  .in_offset                  ->   Transition.in_offset
  .out_offset                 ->   Transition.out_offset
  .parameters                 ->   Transition.metadata.memory_engine

 MediaRef                     -> otio.schema.ExternalReference
  .available_range            ->   ExternalReference.available_range
  .media_id (BLAKE3)          ->   ExternalReference.metadata.memory_engine
                                     .media_id
  (resolved local path)       ->   ExternalReference.target_url, written as a
                                   file:// URL AT EXPORT TIME ONLY. The EDL
                                   itself stores no paths -- it is portable
                                   between machines precisely because it
                                   addresses content by hash. On import the
                                   hash in metadata wins over target_url.

 CONVENTIONS THAT KEEP THE ROUND TRIP EXACT

 - A plain cut is the ABSENCE of a Transition, matching OTIO, where adjacent
   clips simply butt together. Never emit a zero-length Transition for a cut.
 - Transitions sit between their two neighbours in the items list and overlap
   them by in_offset/out_offset. A TRANSITION DOES NOT CHANGE EITHER
   NEIGHBOUR'S TIMELINE EXTENT: the blend straddles the cut, covering the
   outgoing clip's last in_offset frames and the incoming clip's first
   out_offset frames, and the extra frames it needs beyond each clip's
   source_range are the HANDLES, drawn from available_range on either side.
   (This corrected an earlier statement here that the source_ranges already
   included the handles. They do not, in the golden fixture or in
   workers/render-video, and under that reading the fixture's timeline does
   not sum to the 899 frames its own validation report claims -- which is the
   arithmetic every beat lock in it depends on. See contracts#52.)
 - `timeline_range` on a Clip is derived (it is the running sum of preceding
   clip and gap EXTENTS -- see TimeEffect for what an extent is under a speed
   change -- and a transition does not subtract from it) and is NOT exported -- OTIO computes
   it. It is carried here only so a validator can catch a planner that emitted
   an inconsistent timeline, and it is excluded from the determinism digest.
 - Every RationalTime on a video track should share the timeline `rate`.
   Audio-track times may use the audio sample rate. OTIO permits mixed rates;
   this contract permits them only in that one place.

 See docs/otio-mapping.md for the exporter/importer pseudocode and the
 round-trip test plan.

edl_id.description: BLAKE3 over the canonical JSON of this EDL with the volatile fields removed. Two EDLs with the same id render identically.
edl_id.$comment:
THE ID MUST RECOMPUTE, OR IT IS NOT AN ID

 Canonical JSON is RFC 8785: keys sorted by UTF-16 code unit, no insignificant
 whitespace, numbers in ECMAScript Number::toString form (so 120.0 serialises
 as `120`), UTF-8 bytes. Exactly these five paths are removed before hashing,
 and no others:

   edl_id                          -- an id cannot cover itself
   determinism.generated_at        -- a wall clock would change the id per run
   validation.validated_at         -- ditto
   tracks[].items[].timeline_range -- derived, and excluded so re-deriving it
                                      never changes the id
   variant.sibling_edl_ids         -- each sibling's id would otherwise depend
                                      on every other sibling's

 The list is here rather than in one planner's docstring because the id is the
 render-cache key: a consumer that excludes a different set computes a
 different id for the same plan and silently misses the cache, or worse, hits
 it. contracts/tests recomputes it for every golden EDL -- an identity that is
 asserted rather than computed is how issue #26's invented span_id happened.

rate.description: Timeline rate in units per second. All video-track RationalTimes are expressed at this rate. Use exact NTSC rationals where the source demands it (30000/1001), never the rounded decimal.

global_start_time.description: Timeline zero, exported as OTIO Timeline.global_start_time. Normally 0; non-zero when the output must carry a broadcast start timecode such as 01:00:00:00.

media_refs.description: Every source this EDL touches, addressed by content hash. Declared once at the top so a renderer can resolve, verify and pre-open all sources before it starts, and so a missing source is a clean up-front failure rather than a crash at 80%.

tracks.description: Ordered tracks. Index 0 is the bottom video layer, matching OTIO Stack ordering.

reframe_tracks.description: Crop/reframe keyframe tracks, referenced by clips. Held at EDL level rather than inline on the clip so one subject-lock track can drive several clips from the same source shot.

variant.description: Present when this EDL is one of several alternatives offered to the user. The reel planner emits 3-5; whichever the user picks becomes a PrefEvent, and the losers are training signal too.

RenderTarget.title: RenderTarget
RenderTarget.description: What this cut is for. Destination is part of the plan because the reframe, the loudness target and the duration are all chosen for it -- an Instagram cut is not a YouTube cut at a different bitrate.

target_duration.description: What the planner was asked for. The realised duration is the sum of the timeline and may differ slightly, because landing a cut on a beat matters more than hitting exactly 30.000s.

max_duration.description: Hard ceiling imposed by the platform. Exceeding it is a validation failure, not a warning.

loudness_target_lufs.description: Integrated loudness the mix is normalised to. -14 for most social platforms, -23 for broadcast-style masters.

MediaRef.title: MediaRef
MediaRef.description: One source, addressed by content hash rather than by path. This is what makes an EDL portable: the same plan renders on any machine that has the same footage, wherever it happens to live.

media_ref_id.description: Local alias used by clips within this EDL.

media_id.description: BLAKE3 of the source file, i.e. a MediaRecord primary key. For chaptered footage this is the span ASSEMBLY id; the renderer expands it to the ordered member files.

available_range.description: The full extent of the source, in source time. Exported as ExternalReference.available_range. A clip whose source_range escapes this is invalid and must fail validation before render, not during it.

is_span_assembly.description: True when media_id names a virtual assembly of chaptered files rather than a single file on disk.

label.description: Human-readable name for the NLE bin. Cosmetic only -- never used for resolution.

kind.description: Maps to OTIO Track.kind, which recognises exactly "Video" and "Audio".

role.description: What the track is for. Purely ours -- it rides in metadata -- but it lets the renderer build the filtergraph without inspecting contents.

items.description: Ordered children. Clips and gaps tile the track; transitions sit between two neighbours and overlap them.

source_range.description: In and out in SOURCE time, half-open. The single most important field in the contract: it is what the renderer seeks to, and it must round-trip through OTIO unchanged.

timeline_range.description: Derived position on the timeline. Carried for validation only; excluded from the determinism digest and not exported to OTIO, which recomputes it. Its DURATION is derived from source_range and any time_effect by the rule in TimeEffect's $comment -- equal to source_range.duration when there is no effect -- and its START is the running sum of the extents before it. A timeline_range that disagrees with that arithmetic is a validation failure, never a correction.

moment_id.description: The MomentRecord this clip realises. The provenance link that lets 'more of her' re-plan against the same candidate pool instead of starting over.

reframe_track_id.description: Reframe track driving this clip's crop. Null means full frame, letterboxed or pillarboxed per the target.

beat_lock.description: Present when this clip's in-point was snapped to the beat grid. Carries the alignment error so the <50ms quality gate is measurable from the plan alone, without rendering anything.

story_beat_id.description: Which story-arc beat this clip satisfies. Null on clips that are connective tissue rather than a required beat.

Gap.title: Gap
Gap.description: Explicit silence or black. Modelled explicitly, exactly as OTIO does, so a hold at the end of a film is a stated intention rather than an accident of arithmetic.

Transition.title: Transition
Transition.description: An overlap between the two neighbouring items. A hard cut is the absence of one of these, never a zero-length instance -- that is OTIO's convention and departing from it breaks the round trip.

transition_type.description: `dissolve` maps to OTIO's standard SMPTE_Dissolve. Everything else maps to OTIO "Custom" with the specific kind preserved in metadata, which is how OTIO itself handles non-standard transitions.

in_offset.description: How far the transition extends backwards into the outgoing item.

out_offset.description: How far it extends forwards into the incoming item.

parameters.description: Kind-specific settings, e.g. wipe angle. Free-form because the set is open-ended; it rides in OTIO metadata untouched.

TimeEffect.title: TimeEffect
TimeEffect.description: Speed change. Restricted to what OTIO models natively, because a speed ramp that cannot round-trip is a speed ramp that silently disappears in Resolve. `source_range` stays authoritative under an effect and the timeline extent is derived from it -- see the $comment, which is the rule the renderer implements.
TimeEffect.$comment:
WHICH FIELD IS AUTHORITATIVE UNDER A TIME EFFECT (contracts#50)

 `Clip.source_range` is ALWAYS authoritative and ALWAYS means media: the
 frames actually read from the source, in the source's own time. It never
 changes meaning because an effect is attached to the clip.
 `Clip.timeline_range` is ALWAYS derived, and a validator recomputes it:

   no time_effect      timeline extent = source_range.duration
   linear_speed        timeline extent = source_range.duration / time_scalar
   freeze_frame        timeline extent = hold_duration

 and the clip's timeline START is, as ever, the running sum of the extents
 before it on the track (transitions do not change any extent -- see the
 top-of-file $comment).

 `time_scalar` keeps OTIO's LinearTimeWarp meaning exactly: it is the ratio
 of MEDIA time to TIMELINE time. 0.5 plays the media at half speed and so
 occupies twice as many timeline frames as it reads; 2.0 plays it at double
 speed and occupies half.

 WORKED EXAMPLE -- linear_speed, at rate 60000/1001

   source_range = { start_time 3062100, duration 56 }
   time_scalar  = 0.5
   => timeline extent = 56 / 0.5 = 112 frames
   The clip reads 56 frames of media and holds the timeline for 112.
   Output frame k of the clip (k = 0 .. 111) draws source frame
     source_range.start_time + floor(k * time_scalar)
   i.e. 3062100, 3062100, 3062101, 3062101, ... Each source frame is shown
   twice; nothing is interpolated, invented or blended. This sampling rule is
   part of the contract because otherwise one renderer duplicates frames and
   another synthesises them, and the two cuts are different footage.

   `time_scalar` must divide evenly: source_range.duration / time_scalar has
   to be a whole number of timeline frames. A plan that lands on a fractional
   frame is a validation failure, never a rounding -- rounding here is how a
   downbeat moves by half a frame per retimed clip.

 WORKED EXAMPLE -- freeze_frame, at rate 60000/1001

   source_range  = { start_time 3062100, duration 1 }
   freeze_at     = 3062100      (must equal source_range.start_time)
   hold_duration = 90
   => the clip reads exactly ONE frame and holds it for 90 timeline frames.
   source_range.duration must be exactly one frame at the timeline rate, so
   `source_range_within_available` still means what it says, and the hold's
   length is stated rather than inferred from a duration that is not one.

 WHY SOURCE AND NOT TIMELINE

 `source_range` is the field the renderer seeks to, and the one whose meaning
 has to survive a re-trim. Letting a speed change silently reinterpret it as
 a timeline extent would mean the same number denotes media on one clip and
 timeline on the next, with nothing in the file to say which -- and the
 failure mode is a cut landing exactly one retime factor late, which looks
 plausible in review.

 OTIO does not settle this: its own duration arithmetic ignores effects, so a
 naive importer that lays clips out by source_range.duration alone will place
 everything after a retimed clip early. That is a visible, immediate error
 rather than a subtle one, and docs/otio-mapping.md carries the export and
 import rule that avoids it.

 AUDIO UNDER A TIME EFFECT

 `audio_handling: mute` means the clip contributes NO ambient bed at all,
 whatever AmbientPlan gains would otherwise apply to it. `resample` plays the
 clip's audio at the same scalar (pitch moves with it); `preserve_pitch`
 time-stretches without moving pitch. Both non-mute modes are declarations a
 renderer may refuse until it can execute them bit-identically.

time_scalar.description: OTIO LinearTimeWarp.time_scalar: the ratio of media time to timeline time. 0.5 is half speed (twice the timeline extent), 2.0 is double. Required for linear_speed, and must divide source_range.duration into a whole number of timeline frames.

freeze_at.description: Source time to hold. Required for freeze_frame, and must equal source_range.start_time -- the frozen frame is the one frame the clip reads.

hold_duration.description: How long the frozen frame is held, in TIMELINE time. Required for freeze_frame, forbidden otherwise: it is the clip's timeline extent, and without it a freeze has a start and no end.

audio_handling.description: What happens to this clip's audio under a speed change. Almost always `mute` for slow motion, because pitch-shifted ambient sounds broken. `mute` suppresses this clip's ambient bed entirely, whatever AmbientPlan says about it.

ColorOp.title: ColorOp
ColorOp.description: A per-clip colour adjustment, planned by the intelligence layer and merely applied by the renderer.

amount.description: Signed, normalised to [-1,1] where 0 is no change. A single normalised scale keeps ops composable and makes 'is this grade aggressive' a question with an answer.

reference_clip_id.description: For match_to_reference: the clip whose look this one is being matched to. Shot-to-shot consistency inside a scene is planned, not left to the encoder.

fade_in.description: Fade length at the clip's in-point. The curve is a LINEAR RAMP IN AMPLITUDE from 0 to 1 over the declared frames -- not equal-power, not linear in dB (contracts#60). Equal-power is the usual choice for a music crossfade and would be audibly different on a long fade, so it is named here rather than left to the mixer; a planner that wants a different shape emits a Transition.

fade_out.description: Fade length ending on the clip's last frame, a linear ramp in amplitude from 1 to 0. Same convention as fade_in.

audio_extends_past_out.description: L-cut: hold this clip's audio past its visual out-point, so a laugh finishes over the next shot. Realises MomentRecord.safe_trim.preserve_audio_tail.

BeatLock.title: BeatLock
BeatLock.description: Records that a cut was placed against the music rather than merely near it. `alignment_error_ms` is the audit trail for the <50ms downbeat quality gate.

alignment_error_ms.description: Signed distance from the clip's timeline in-point to the beat. Negative is early. Non-zero because a cut must also land on a certified snap point, and the nearest snap point is rarely exactly on the beat -- the planner trades a few milliseconds of beat error for a cut that lands on a real motion onset.

snap_point_kind.description: Which MomentRecord snap point the cut actually landed on.

Marker.title: Marker
Marker.description: Maps to otio.schema.Marker. Markers are how our reasoning becomes visible to a human editor who opens the timeline in Resolve.

ReframeTrack.title: ReframeTrack
ReframeTrack.description: A crop keyframe track that turns landscape footage into a vertical cut with the subject held in frame. This is core IP and has no OTIO equivalent, so it round-trips through metadata.

keyframes.description: Ordered by time, at least one. A single keyframe is a static crop; the interesting case is a moving crop that tracks a subject across the frame.

fallback.description: What to do if subject tracking fails at render time. Never leave this implicit: a reframe that silently falls back to a centre crop can decapitate the subject of the shot.

time.description: SOURCE time of the keyframe, so the track stays valid if the clip is later trimmed or retimed.

crop.description: Crop window in normalised source coordinates. Its aspect must match the track's target_aspect_ratio; a mismatch is a validation failure because the renderer must not be the one deciding how to reconcile it.

interpolation.description: How to reach the NEXT keyframe. `hold` produces a snap, which is occasionally what a hard beat wants. Every mode is a stated formula, not a name -- see the $comment.
interpolation.$comment:
INTERPOLATION IS A FORMULA, NOT AN ADJECTIVE (contracts#51)

 Let the keyframes of a track be K[0..n-1] with strictly increasing source
 times t[0..n-1] and crop values P[0..n-1]. Each component of the crop box
 (x, y, w, h) is interpolated INDEPENDENTLY and identically. For a source
 frame f with t[i] <= f < t[i+1], let

   u = (f - t[i]) / (t[i+1] - t[i])          -- so u is in [0, 1)

 and let the mode be the one declared on K[i] (the keyframe being left, not
 the one being reached).

   linear  value = P[i] + (P[i+1] - P[i]) * u

   hold    value = P[i]   for every f in the interval. The snap happens at
           t[i+1], where the next interval takes over.

   bezier  A cubic Bezier easing with P0=(0,0) and P3=(1,1) and the two
           `bezier_control` points as P1 and P2, in (time, value) normalised
           keyframe-interval space -- CSS's cubic-bezier(). Solve x(s) = u for
           s, then value = P[i] + (P[i+1] - P[i]) * y(s).

   smooth  A UNIFORM Catmull-Rom spline through the keyframe values, endpoints
           clamped. With

             A = P[i-1], clamped to P[i]   when i == 0
             B = P[i]
             C = P[i+1]
             D = P[i+2], clamped to P[i+1] when i+2 > n-1

           value = 0.5 * ( (2*B)
                         + (-A + C) * u
                         + (2*A - 5*B + 4*C - D) * u^2
                         + (-A + 3*B - 3*C + D) * u^3 )

 WHY THIS CURVE, AND WHY UNIFORM

 `smooth` is what a subject-tracking crop wants: it is C1 at every interior
 keyframe, so the crop has no visible velocity step where one keyframe hands
 over to the next, and it passes exactly through every keyframe, so the
 positions the planner stated are the positions rendered.

 CLAMPING THE ENDPOINTS IS AN EASE, NOT A STRAIGHT LINE. The tangent at K[i]
 is (P[i+1] - P[i-1]) / 2; with P[-1] clamped to P[0] that is half the first
 segment's slope, so the crop eases into the track and out of it rather than
 starting at full speed. On a TWO-keyframe track the whole path is that ease:

   value = B + (C - B) * (0.5*u + 1.5*u^2 - u^3)

 which passes through both keyframes, is monotone (its derivative,
 0.5 + 3u - 3u^2, has a minimum of 0.5 on [0,1]), never leaves [B, C], and
 reaches the midpoint at u = 0.5. It is NOT a lerp -- a planner that wants a
 constant-velocity pan asks for `linear`.

 UNIFORM means the tangents are built from neighbouring VALUES only; the
 spacing of t[] does not enter the formula. The centripetal variant is better
 behaved on unevenly spaced keyframes, and it is rejected here for one
 reason: it needs a fourth root of a distance, and pow() is not bit-identical
 across platforms and libms. The uniform form uses only +, - and *, so every
 conforming implementation lands on the same IEEE-754 double, which is what
 `edl_id` promises. A planner that wants spacing-aware easing has `bezier`,
 whose curve it states explicitly.

 Catmull-Rom overshoots: between two keyframes the value can leave the
 interval [P[i], P[i+1]]. That is the point (it is what makes the motion look
 like a camera move rather than a series of ramps) and it is the PLANNER's
 job to keep the interpolated path inside the frame. A renderer that finds a
 crop leaving the source frame fails; it does not clamp, because a clamp is
 how a crop silently slides off its subject.

 Interpolation is evaluated against integer SOURCE frame numbers, never
 against seconds, so a retimed clip (see TimeEffect) samples the same curve
 at the source frames it actually reads.

bezier_control.description: Control points for bezier interpolation, as (x,y) in normalised keyframe-interval space.

confidence.description: Tracker confidence at this keyframe. Low-confidence stretches are where the fallback earns its keep.

subject_ref.description: The tracked entity: a SAM 2 object id, a face track uuid, or null for saliency.

keep_in_frame.description: The part of the subject that must never leave the crop. `head` is the one that matters for people: a technically-centred crop that clips a forehead reads as a mistake.

headroom.description: Fraction of the crop height kept above the subject's head. Composition rule, planned rather than hard-coded in the renderer.

ReframeSmoothing.title: ReframeSmoothing
ReframeSmoothing.description: Constraints that stop a reframe from looking like a nervous camera operator. Raw per-frame subject centroids are far too jittery to use directly.

max_velocity_per_second.description: Cap on crop travel, in normalised units per second. The difference between a considered pan and a whip.

deadzone.description: Subject movement smaller than this does not move the crop at all, which is what keeps a mostly-still subject from causing constant micro-drift.

AudioPlan.title: AudioPlan
AudioPlan.description: The complete audio intention: what music plays, how much of the original scene survives under it, and how the two are balanced against each other over time.

ducking.description: Ordered ducking rules. Later rules win where they overlap, which keeps the resolution deterministic instead of depending on the renderer's mixer implementation.

MusicCue.title: MusicCue
MusicCue.description: Licence and provenance for one piece of music, attached to the clips that place it. A cue is NOT a placement: the bed lives on an audio track like every other sound, and the cue says what it is and what may legally be done with it.
MusicCue.$comment:
MUSIC IS PLACED ONCE (contracts#59)

 This type used to carry `source_range`, `timeline_range`, `gain_db`,
 `fade_in` and `fade_out` as well as a licence, which meant a well-formed EDL
 described the same bed twice: once as an audio-track Clip and once here. A
 renderer that summed them played the music 6 dB hot; a renderer that read
 one of them was guessing which. Both are plausible and neither is loud.

 The track placement is authoritative, for three reasons: it is the
 OTIO-native structure (a Clip on a Track with kind "Audio"), it is what
 survives a round trip into Resolve, and `Track.role` already tells the mixer
 which bed is music without inspecting its contents. So the cue keeps only
 what a placement cannot express -- the licence -- plus `clip_ids`, which
 says which placements it covers.

 LOOPING (contracts#57)

 There is deliberately no `loop` flag. A bed that has to cover more timeline
 than the track offers is emitted as SEVERAL clips, one per pass, each with
 its own source_range and timeline_range and each listed in `clip_ids`. The
 loop join is then an ordinary cut between two ordinary clips: its restart
 point is visible in the plan, its truncation is visible in the plan, and a
 crossfade across the join -- if the planner wants one -- is an ordinary
 Transition. A boolean could express none of that, and every unstated part of
 it (butt or crossfade, restart at the cue's in-point or the track's start,
 truncate or overrun) moves the bed against the BeatGrid, which is the one
 thing every beat-locked cut in the timeline depends on.

 `BeatGrid.source_cue_id` still names a cue, and the grid is still authored
 in timeline time, so the anchor resolves exactly as before.

media_ref_id.description: The source this cue licenses. Must equal the media_ref_id of every clip in clip_ids.

clip_ids.description: The audio-track clips that place this cue, in timeline order. One entry for a bed that plays once, one per pass for a bed that repeats. Every clip on a track whose role is `music` must be claimed by exactly one cue -- that is how an unlicensed bed becomes impossible rather than merely unlikely.

license.description: Required, not optional. Music licensing is a Phase 0 decision precisely because an unlicensed track in a shared reel is a legal problem, and the plan is the place it becomes checkable.

cleared_for.description: Where this cut may legally be published. `user_supplied` music is typically personal_use only, and a share flow must be able to refuse rather than discover the problem after upload.

AmbientPlan.title: AmbientPlan
AmbientPlan.description: How much of the original location sound survives. Keeping real ambient under music is most of what separates a film that feels like a memory from a slideshow with a soundtrack.

preserve_speech.description: When true, clips containing speech keep their ambient at full level and the music ducks under them instead.

high_pass_hz.description: Removes wind rumble, which otherwise dominates every outdoor action clip.

DuckingRule.title: DuckingRule
DuckingRule.description: One sidechain relationship, expressed as intent (duck music under speech by 9dB) rather than as a rendered gain curve, so the renderer stays dumb and the decision stays auditable.

trigger.description: What turns it down. `explicit_ranges` means the planner decided the ranges itself rather than relying on detection at render time -- always preferred, because it is deterministic.

reduction_db.description: Positive number of dB to reduce by.

ranges.description: Timeline ranges the rule applies over. Required when trigger is explicit_ranges; when empty with another trigger, the rule applies for the whole timeline.

BeatGrid.title: BeatGrid
BeatGrid.description: The musical skeleton the cut is hung on. Stored as explicit per-beat times rather than as a BPM to be extrapolated, because real tracks drift and an extrapolated grid is 200ms out by the end of a 30-second reel.

beats.description: Every beat, in TIMELINE time, ordered. Downbeats are flagged rather than stored separately so a cut can reference one index regardless of which it turned out to be.

analyzer.description: Which beat tracker produced this. Recorded partly for reproducibility and partly because the licence-safe analyser (librosa, ISC) and the more accurate but non-commercial ones (madmom) must never be confused.

tolerance_ms.description: Maximum acceptable beat-alignment error for a cut claiming to be beat-locked. The quality gate is 50ms on downbeats.

section.description: Musical section this beat falls in. Lets the planner put the visual peak on the drop rather than merely on a loud beat.

StoryArc.title: StoryArc
StoryArc.description: The narrative intention, kept with the plan so that a revision instruction such as 'more of her' or 'less drone' re-satisfies the SAME arc instead of re-planning from scratch. That persistence is what makes iterative editing feel like direction rather than dice-rolling.

logline.description: One sentence the arc is trying to say. Written by the frontier model and shown to the user, so a plan can be judged before it is rendered.

energy_curve.description: Target energy over the timeline, as sampled control points. The planner satisfies it mechanically by choosing moments whose features match; it is a specification, not a description.

source.description: Who authored the arc. A tier3_model arc must carry its ConsentRef, because producing it meant sending a contact sheet off the device.

prompt_id.description: Which prompt-engine template produced it, so a prompt regression is traceable to the outputs it affected.

rationale.description: The model's stated reasoning, kept for the user-facing 'why this cut' explanation and for eval review.

intent.description: What this act is for, in plain language: 'arrival, establish where we are'.

StoryBeat.title: StoryBeat
StoryBeat.description: A required narrative element and the clips that satisfy it. An unsatisfied required beat is a validation failure -- that is the mechanism by which 'the film has an arc' is checked rather than hoped for.

candidate_moment_ids.description: Moments the planner considered for this beat. Retained so a revision can swap in an alternative without re-running retrieval.

tone_map_hdr_to_sdr.description: Required when any source is HLG or PQ and the target is SDR. Left implicit, HDR sources render washed out.

strategy.description: What was varied. Variants must differ along a stated axis, so the user's pick is interpretable as a preference rather than as noise.

description.description: One line the variant picker shows: 'faster, more action'.

EdlValidation.title: EdlValidation
EdlValidation.description: Result of the pre-render checks. The renderer refuses an EDL that has not passed, which keeps 'the renderer is dumb' from meaning 'the renderer is trusting'.

OtioExportInfo.title: OtioExportInfo
OtioExportInfo.description: Bookkeeping for the OTIO round trip. `unmapped_fields` must be empty for an export to be called lossless; if it is not, the exporter is telling us exactly which part of the contract has outgrown the mapping.

round_trip_verified.description: Set by the exporter after re-importing its own output and comparing to the source EDL. The claim of losslessness is tested per export, not assumed.
